extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers / chymists and readers evaluating alchemical/chymical claims (17th-century scientists or historians of scientific method)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for assessing claims, experiments, and doctrines in chymistry/alchemy — focusing on evidence, reproducible processes, definitions of 'elements', and avoidance of imposture or ambiguous terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be impressed by hard names or bold assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: "must not suffer our Selves to be impos'd upon by hard Names, or bold Assertions; nor to be dazl'd by that Light which should but assist us to discern things the more clearly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: accepting claims because of learned-sounding terminology or authoritative tone. Require that claims stand on demonstrable evidence rather than rhetorical flourish or mysterious language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish production from understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is one thing to be able to help Nature to produce things, and another thing to Understand well the Nature of the things produc'd."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An experiment that produces an effect (e.g., a new-looking substance) is insufficient to prove understanding of its nature; further analysis and demonstration of composition are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not generalize a universal number of elements without proof
rubrics_metrics.description: "it does not appear, that Three is precisely and Universally the Number of the Distinct Substances or Elements, whereinto mixt Bodies are resoluble by the Fire"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require empirical demonstrations across a wide range of bodies before asserting a universal principle (e.g., Tria Prima). Beware of extrapolating from limited examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require intelligible, practicable, and reproducible processes
rubrics_metrics.description: "I must take the Liberty to refrain from believing it, till the Chymists prove it, or give us intelligible and practicable Processes to performe what they pretend."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must be described clearly enough to be repeated; opaque or 'ænigmatical' procedures undermine confidence. Prefer stepwise, reproducible protocols and open methods over secretive recipes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for reagents/menstruums producing the observed products
rubrics_metrics.description: "it will remain doubtful... whether the Emergent Salt be that of the Gold it self; or of the Saline Bodies or Spirits employ'd to prepare it"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design controls to show that any separated substance originates from the tested material rather than from corrosives, solvents, or additives (example: apparent 'salts' or crystals may be mixtures formed with aqua fortis or other corrosive liquors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against imposture, trickery, and self-deception
rubrics_metrics.description: "they have often seen Detected many tricks and Impostures of Cheating Alchymists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require skillful, circumspect observation and independent verification; be skeptical of results from unskilful or credulous observers. Example: Carneades' staged experiment producing 'mercury' from a prepared mixture to show how easily observers may be deceived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand competent testimony and credible eyewitness verification
rubrics_metrics.description: "neither my own Experiments, nor any competent Testimony hath hitherto either taught me how such an Analysis may be made"; "the relation of any credible eye witnesse."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer observations attested by competent practitioners and reproducible by others. Anecdotal or single, unverifiable reports are insufficient to establish chemical facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equivocal terminology; define principles consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: Chymists "call the same Substance, sometimes the Sulphur, and Sometimes the Mercury of a Body."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific claims require clear, consistent names and definitions. Ambiguous use of terms (naming one thing several ways or several things the same) obscures meaning and impedes evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: To call something an 'element' show it is uncompounded
rubrics_metrics.description: "whether each of these be un-compounded, I reserve to examine..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling a substance as elemental requires evidence it cannot be further resolved into distinct constituents; do not assume elemental status merely because the usual analyses stop there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify elements by ingredienthood, not by usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Elements being call'd so in relation to the constituting of mixt Bodies, it should be upon the account of its Ingrediency, not of its use"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether something is an element based on whether it is a genuine constituent of the compound, rather than on whether it is active or useful to humans or practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for sensory and instrumental limitations; suspect invisible constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: "there may be severall Sorts of Bodies, which are not Immediate Objects of any one of our senses"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that certain constituents may escape detection by ordinary senses or crude apparatus. Design experiments and apparatus to detect subtle or volatile fractions and be cautious about declaring homogeneity from purely sensory observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate chemical methods/reagents to separate and test distinct substances
rubrics_metrics.description: Carneades' separation of an acid spirit and a non-acid spirit from box-wood using coral: the acid spirit dissolved coral and reacted differently with reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose separating agents and tests based on expected chemical behaviours (acid/base reactions, solubility, reactivity with lead, colour changes, boiling/hissing). Validate distinctness by differential reactivity and recovery tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer practical, economically feasible demonstrations and independent replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Carneades invites a trial for separating gold into Salt, Sulphur and Mercury but refuses to risk costly unsatisfactory trials: "the materials that must be wrought upon are somewhat too pretious and costly to be wasted upon so groundlesse adventures"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary claims should be supported by demonstrations that others can reasonably reproduce; impractical, very costly, or unreproducible demonstrations are weak evidence unless independently replicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about general claims from limited experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples given where some bodies yield fewer than three 'principles' and others more; "it may without Absurdity be Question'd..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid asserting sweeping universal doctrines (e.g., a fixed set of principles for all bodies) when observations show variability; let classification be guided by cumulative, varied experimental results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate clearly; avoid intentional obscurity to feign depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Chymists "write darkly" and may do so not because notions are too precious but because they fear men would discern they are far from precious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good scientific practice includes plain, candid exposition. Obscure writing that appears intended to awe rather than inform should be treated as a red flag regarding the solidity of claims.
